U(1) R symmetry breaking in the 4D effective theory is a natural consequence of the compactification of a 6D theory.
U(1) R mediation is a viable candidate for the SUSY breaking in a fluxed 6D supergravity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 6D flux compactification with U(1)D-brane provides a new framework to realize the U(1)-mediated supersymmetry breaking with a non-trivial D-term in the hidden sector.
the supersymmetry breaking is mediated by a combination of the bulk and brane contributions, and the soft scalar masses are dominantly generated by a brane contribution.
the U(1)_R symmetry is broken at a scale comparable with the gravitino mass, which is a consequence of the U(1)\_(R) D-term contribution to the soft masses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the U(1)(B-L) gauge symmetry is broken by the flux compactification in the hidden sector, and the U(1)_R gauge symmetry is broken in the visible sector.
the U(1)_R D-term contribution to the soft scalar masses can be comparable to the U(1)^3 D-term contribution.
